'''Sir Colin John Humphreys''' (born 24 May 1941) is a British [[physicist]] and a hobbyist Bible scholar.<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref> He is the Professor of Materials Science at [[Queen Mary University of London]]. 

He is the former Goldsmiths' Professor of Materials Science at the University of Cambridge and the Professor of Experimental Physics at the [[Royal Institution]] in London. He served as President of the [[Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining]] in 2002 and 2003. His research interests include "all aspects of [[electron microscopy]] and analysis, semiconductors (particularly [[gallium nitride]]), ultra-high temperature aerospace materials and [[superconductors]]."<ref name=cam>University of Cambridge, [http://www-hrem.msm.cam.ac.uk/people/humphreys/ Colin Humphreys] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100110223853/http://www-hrem.msm.cam.ac.uk/people/humphreys/ |date=10 January 2010 }}</ref> Humphreys also "studies the Bible when not pursuing his day-job as a [[materials scientist]]."<ref>{{cite web | url= http://www.cam.ac.uk/research/news/the-penultimate-supper/ | title= The Penultimate Supper? | date= 17 April 2011 | publisher= Cambridge University| access-date=2011-04-23 | quote= The new study is based on earlier research which Professor Humphreys carried out with the Oxford astrophysicist, Graeme Waddington, in 1983. This identified the date of Jesus' crucifixion as the morning of Friday, April 3rd, AD 33 – which has since been widely accepted by other scholars as well. For Professor Humphreys, who only studies the Bible when not pursuing his day-job as a materials scientist, this presented an opportunity to deal with the equally difficult issue of when (and how) Jesus' Last Supper really took place.}}</ref>

==Education==
Humphreys was educated at [[Luton Sixth Form College|Luton Grammar School]],<ref name=whoswho/> [[Imperial College London]] (BSc) and [[Churchill College, Cambridge]]<ref name=whoswho/> where he was awarded a [[PhD]] in 1969.<ref name=cjPhD>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|url=https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/35300297?style=html|title=Aspects of multiple beam electron diffraction and X-ray diffraction topography|first= Colin John|last=Humphreys|date=1969|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.604776}}|website=jisc.ac.uk|oclc=885437201}}</ref> He was awarded a [[Master of Arts]] degree from [[Jesus College, Oxford]].<ref name=whoswho/>{{clarify|date=November 2018}}

==Career and research==

=== Semiconductors ===
Humphreys is a materials scientist who has carried out work on the electron microscopy of semiconducting materials. His research on [[gallium nitride]] (GaN) has resulted in a substantially improved understanding of this material with a wide range of technological applications.<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/colin-humphreys-11662/|website=royalsociety.org|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|author=Anon|year=2011|title=Sir Colin Humphreys CBE FREng FRS}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|“All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]].” --{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/|title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies|date=2016-11-11}}}}</ref>

In addition to its potential use within transistors as a next-generation alternative to silicon, GaN emits a brilliant light that makes it an ideal candidate for use in energy-saving [[LED]]s.<ref name=frs/> Colin has pioneered the development of low-cost, high-efficiency GaN-on-silicon (or ‘GaN-on-Si’) LEDs, which are now being manufactured based on his patented research.<ref name=frs/> GaN LED lighting could save the United Kingdom £2 billion per year in electricity costs.<ref name=frs/>

Humphreys is a member of the [[John Templeton Foundation]].<ref name=cam/> and a member of the Advisory Council for the [[Campaign for Science and Engineering]].<ref name="CaSE Advisory Council">{{cite web |url=http://www.sciencecampaign.org.uk/about/who/advisory.htm |title=Advisory Council of the Campaign for Science and Engineering |access-date=2011-02-11 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100828110110/http://www.sciencecampaign.org.uk/about/who/advisory.htm |archive-date=2010-08-28 }}</ref>

===Biblical studies===
====Date of Last Supper====
In 2011, Humphreys claimed in his book ''The Mystery of the Last Supper'' that the [[Last Supper]] took place on Wednesday ([[Holy Wednesday]]), not as traditionally thought Thursday ([[Maundy Thursday]]), and that the apparent timing discrepancies ([[Nisan]] 15 or 14) between the gospels of Matthew, Mark, and Luke versus John are rooted in the use of different calendars by the writers. Mark, Matthew and Luke appear to use an older, Egyptian-style Jewish calendar (still used today by the [[Samaritans]]) while John appears to refer to the newer, Babylonian-style Jewish calendar (still in use by modern [[Jews]]).<ref>Humphreys, Colin J. The Mystery of the Last Supper : Reconstructing the Final Days of Jesus. Cambridge: Cambridge Univ. Press, 2011, p193.</ref> The Last Supper being on Wednesday would allow more time for interrogation and presentation to Pilate prior to the crucifixion on Friday than given in the traditional view. Humphreys proposed the actual date for the Last Supper to be 1 April 33.<ref>Humphreys, Colin J. The Mystery of the Last Supper : Reconstructing the Final Days of Jesus. Cambridge: Cambridge Univ. Press, 2011, p164.</ref>

====Eclipse made "sun stand still"====
In a 2017 paper written together with Graeme Waddington, Humphreys offered an astronomical explanation for the [[Hebrew Bible|biblical]] story of the sun standing still over [[Gibeon (ancient city)|Gibeon]] during the [[Israelites]]' victorious battle against the [[Amorites]] ({{bibleverse|Joshua|10:12}}), namely an annular eclipse which occurred on 30 October 1207 BCE.<ref name=Humphreys>{{cite journal |last1= Humphreys |first1= Colin |author-link1= Colin Humphreys |last2= Waddington |first2= Graeme |title= Solar eclipse of 1207 BC helps to date pharaohs |journal= Astronomy & Geophysics |volume= 58| issue = 5 |date= 1 October 2017 |pages= 5.39–5.42 |doi= 10.1093/astrogeo/atx178 |url= https://academic.oup.com/astrogeo/article/58/5/5.39/4159289 |access-date= 18 March 2021|doi-access= free }}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=December 2022}}

==Awards and honours==
Humphreys was elected in 1996 as a [[Fellow]]<ref name="List of Fellows">{{cite web|title=List of Fellows|website=raeng.org.uk|url=http://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/people-council-committees/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows|access-date=20 October 2014|archive-date=8 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160608094405/http://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/people-council-committees/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref> of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]]<ref name="List of Fellows"/>
He won the [[Institute of Physics]] [[Kelvin Medal and Prize]] in 2000.
Humphreys was awarded the [[A. A. Griffith Medal and Prize]] in 2001 and a [[CBE]] in 2003 for services to science as a researcher and communicator.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/story.asp?storycode=173836 |title= New year honours |work= Times Higher Education |date= 3 January 2003 |access-date=2011-04-23}}</ref>
He was [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] in the [[2010 Birthday Honours]]<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=59446 |date=12 June 2010 |page=1 |supp=y}}</ref> and in 2011 elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref>{{cite web | url =http://royalsociety.org/people/colin-humphreys/ |title = Sir Colin John Humphreys CBE FREng FRS| publisher = Royal Society|access-date = 2010-03-18}}</ref>
In 2015 he was elected as an [[Honorary Fellow of the Royal Microscopical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Honorary Fellows|url=http://www.rms.org.uk/membership/honorary-fellows.html|website=[[Royal Microscopical Society]]|access-date=20 February 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Honorary Fellows Past and Present|url=http://www.rms.org.uk/membership/honorary-fellows/past-honorary-fellows.html|website=[[Royal Microscopical Society]]|access-date=20 February 2017}}</ref>
He is also mentioned in Debrett's People of Today.<ref>[http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/search/results/14261/Colin%20John%20HUMPHREYS.aspx Sir Colin Humphreys on Debrett's People of Today]</ref>{{when|date=January 2020}}
